tws-soundpeats-clearpods.review: Lacking. The driver isn't pleasant. Just get the K20i.

tws-soundpeats-air3.review: Has aptX and a gaming mode for games, and above all it uses NO EARTIPS. For people who like the AirPods style, this is the answer.

tws-nakamichi-tws1xs.review: Earbuds. Warm. The mic isn't great and neither is the battery. For earbuds the sound is decent enough for bargain hunters.

tws-robot-flybuds-t50.review: An upgrade of the T10 with a longer battery, and slightly better sound too.

tws-robot-flybuds-t10.review: If you want a cheap TWS, better to look for one like this: a 1-year replace-with-new warranty. Earbud shape, for those who've been looking for one without rubber eartips. Bluetooth 5.3, 25-hour battery.

tws-lenovo-lp1-pro.review: The sound isn't good. But if you really need earbuds like this, go ahead. It's a bit tinny, somehow.

tws-shokz-openfit-pro.tagline: King of open-ear earhooks, with light ANC
tws-shokz-openfit-pro.review: Finally the king is back, claiming the top spot. Has ANC. A good mic even in windy conditions, a clear, distortion-free driver, cleaner clarity than the Aerofit 2. You can thicken the bass with EQ too. And the vocals are excellent: detailed, spacious. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-huawei-freeclip-2.review: The loudest driver of all the clip-ons I've tried, Sony included. Clarity is very clear compared with the LinkBuds Clip. Better mic too. More in his video review.

tws-bose-ultra-open-earbuds-2nd-gen.review: Good driver. The deepest lows of the clip-on style; not as bright as Huawei or Oppo. Unique colours. 3-band EQ. Beyond that I'm not sure what else to discuss. Not bad, but 4 million rupiah, man.

tws-oppo-enco-clip-2.review: The best-sounding clip-on, tuned by Dynaudio. Only preset EQs, no custom, but the presets are already very good. I use Dynamic, tuned in the direction of Dynaudio's speaker house sound, with the deepest sub-bass of any clip-on open-ear. Pure Vocal is also good if you like vocal/mid-centric sound with less air and sub.

tws-soundcore-aerofit-2.review: Very good. You can feel the bass. The battery lasts a long time too. High value for money: only a million rupiah but genuinely good for an open-ear. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-shokz-openfit-2.review: Good. Very balanced without EQ. App support is OK. Can match the Aerofit 2; a very premium sound. Only the price is too high, since the Aerofit 2 is that cheap. The fit locks over the ear better than the Aerofit.

tws-sony-linkbuds-clip.review: A Sony driver is never going to be muffled: clear, detailed, a very spacious soundstage. But of course it still suffers from a lack of loudness and bass outdoors. Indoors in a quiet place it's very good: spacious soundstage, nice Sony timbre, a clear driver. There's a 10-band EQ, but you can't push the bass very far. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-sony-linkbuds-open.review: You can feel the bass for an open design. The fit has nothing dangling behind the ear, no neckband. A driver with a hole in it: very unique, nothing else like it. Shame it's expensive. Main weakness: the treble isn't as detailed as the Aerofit; the Aerofit is very good and already has LDAC, this doesn't. (Video review on his YouTube.)

tws-xiaomi-openwear-stereo-pro.review: KING OF OPEN-EAR MICS. 1 piezo, 1 DD, 2 BA, like an IEM! But it still sounds like an open-ear: less sub-bass, a bit less bass than the Aerofit. The highs are crisp, sparkling, shimmering and clear, but there's not much body from low-mids down to sub. The Aerofit 2 is still better if bass outdoors is your priority; indoors this is still fine. (Video review on his YouTube.)

tws-earfun-clip-2.review: A little bright, but the mic has improved and there's a custom EQ, so you can lower the treble to be safer. Good price, and physical buttons.

tws-soundpeats-pearlclip-pro.review: Surprisingly good. And CHEAP! That's what matters. For an inexpensive open-ear, no need for luxury; it's like wearing an open-back headphone, but the sound is very natural. Not much bass, but definitely more extended than the Moondrop Pill.

tws-huawei-freearc.review: It's OK, safe. Has an EQ too. Not a bad product. But the Soundcore Aerofit 2 has better separation and bass. The mic, oh, really weak; far behind Xiaomi. The app needs an APK downloaded from Huawei: not complicated, just not through Google Play.

tws-earfun-open-jump.review: Better than the V20i, but not as amazing as the Aerofit 2. Sound is OK. You won't regret it.

tws-audio-technica.review: Like the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, except it isn't bone conduction against the skull but cartilage conduction, on the soft cartilage at the front of the ear. Good. Has EQ. But it's as expensive as Shokz, so it's surely a tough fight. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-soundcore-v20i.review: Won't match the Aerofit 2: the soundstage, clarity, detail and resolution are far apart. But as a secondary open-ear for running or cycling it's still OK. I prefer this to the GoFree. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-edifier-comfo-run.review: A muffled, murky driver; separation isn't great. Far behind the Shokz OpenRun or ATH-CC500BT2 for sound. But the mic is really good.

tws-philips-taq2000.review: The sound is still OK, not too murky, some clarity. Has an app.

tws-moondrop-pill.review: Tonally OK, actually; the bass preset is fine too. But the volume is low, not as loud as EarFun; especially outdoors with traffic noise it's surely not great. Good timbre, good driver, mic not bad. AAC codec.

tws-soundpeats-go-free2.review: OK, fine, since the V30i isn't sold any more. More or less similar. Low-latency mode.

tws-soundcore-v30i.review: The bass really comes through, without overdoing it. Comfortable. Even better than Soundcore's 2-million Aerofit, or even the Sony Float Run.

tws-soundpeats-runfree.review: If you want a neckband style, this is decent. The sound is fairly bassy too.

tws-soundcore-aerofit-pro.review: Expensive, but lots of features. The sound still loses to the V30i though.

tws-sony-floatrun.review: Still OK, still fairly balanced. No weird vibration like Shokz.

tws-huawei-freeclip.review: Very doubtful whether the fit really locks. Scary. The sound is like holding a phone loudspeaker near your ear. Suits cute Y2K-style girls as an accessory.

tws-audio-technica-ac5tw.review: Low volume, no extra volume boost on the TWS, no app. Oof, tough.

iem-xenns-mangird-tea-pro-se.tagline: Highly coherent + superb natural timbre and stereo imaging width
iem-xenns-mangird-tea-pro-se.review: CAN'T GO WRONG WITH Xenns: the best DD and BA implementation, pushed to the max. The timbre is definitely more natural, far less plasticky than the regular Tea Pro. The mid-bass is cleaned up: lowered, but you still feel it. The 2 DDs now rumble just right, not as bassy and slightly muddy as the Tea Pro. Annoyingly, the treble rises again from 6 kHz up, so it's best at medium-to-low volume. The 2 Knowles BAs are upgraded in the highs, but I think the boost should have stayed at the Tea Pro's amount.

iem-hisenior-mega5est-7th.review: You can't go wrong with this set. A bit more sub-bass than the Tea Pro. The treble goes in a similar direction to the Tea Pro SE, but the highs have an appealing smoothness and sharpness. The soundstage up top is indeed wide, but the Tea Pro SE's stereo separation and imaging are wider. The sense of room can compete, but for stereo imaging width the Tea Pro SE is still the champion. Vocals are more forward and cleaner on the Tea Pro SE. This one is good in the highs, but the imaging is still a little centred for the budget.

iem-hisenior-mega7.review: Very much in the same direction as the Tea Pro SE, and the treble isn't as bright and pointy as the Astral. The main reason I prefer the Tea Pro SE: its dynamic drivers are better. The rumble is just right, the punch tactile and bouncy, with mids I find well proportioned. The highs are more or less similar. The main reason to choose this one: the cable is gorgeous, like holding an Eletech or Effect Audio-level cable. Lovely; the material feels like the Eletech Socrates.

iem-mangird-tea-pro.tagline: Holographic imaging and stage (Iga Massardi, Gerald / Barasuara)
iem-mangird-tea-pro.review: ENDGAME UNDER 10 million rupiah for me, subjectively. Coherency better than the Hype 4, Davinci, Oracle 3 and EJ07M. Proper bass, not overdone but still fun compared with the Pilgrim Silver. The vocals stay separate from the bass even though the bass spreads wide, deep and punchy; it doesn't bleed into the vocals. Like a stage PA: bass sent via aux to the sub, vocals stay in the mains. Separation and soundstage better than the Tea 2, with more clarity too. Volume linearity is solid even loud, typical Mangird. Spacious and pleasant. No need to swap the cable (it's detachable). Definitely worth more than its price. (Review on his YouTube.)

iem-yu9-que-melody.review: If you find the upper mids on the Reference or other CrinEars too high, try this. The air is fairly safe too, and the treble is smooth, nothing weird. The Melody has cleaner low-mids than the regular Que.

iem-melody-wings-neptune.review: A very unique configuration. The good bone-conduction driver I found really impressive is in the Canpur CP622B, but I don't put those in the book because they're too expensive for my audience; let's keep it below 10 million. But this is good, tidy. The bass is tight, cushioned, cleaner than the Tea Pro, bouncy but clean, less boomy/bloated, faster than the Tea Pro. The treble is dangerous from 6–8 kHz to 14 kHz, making the treble and air bright. Very good separation; it competes strongly with the Tea Pro. I think the soundstage is slightly better than the Tea Pro. The fit is bigger and fuller in the ear than the Tea Pro.

iem-crinear-reference.tagline: King of mids; the most neutral IEM (B&K 5128 based)
iem-crinear-reference.review: Nicely neutral. Not airy, not much sub-bass. Superb midrange performance. Not for loud-volume lovers who need bass, not for bassheads, not for fun Harman fans. Really mid-centric and vocal-centric. The bass reaches deep but isn't boosted much like the Tea Pro. Why I put it a bit lower: I guarantee fewer people like this kind of neutral, low-bass sound than like a spicy Meta tuning with lots of sub and air, or a Harman-like target. I also feel a low-shelf bass boost from 150 Hz down would make it more fun. Technically the Tea Pro is a bit wider. But the tonality is tidy and I use it everywhere: neutral, tidy, no bright air, so for my daily editing and mixing of my content voiceovers it's fine, and lovely for mixing on the go. (Full review on his YouTube.)

iem-xenns-top-pro.review: Good timbre, good coherency. The only problem for me is the treble: the top end is a bit pointy. If you listen loud and are sensitive above 10 kHz it may be too airy, though some people like this; I don't much. I want the upper mids to treble like JM-1 or a Meta tuning, falling gradually rather than climbing again (see the JM-1 curve on squig.link/lab/fernandagunsan). Overall the timbre is more correct and less plasticky than the Tea Pro, but I don't hear an improvement in imaging or soundstage; the bass and mid-bass are cleaner. If you want something that feels clean and less bassy than the Tea Pro, this could be it. But remember the treble rises at the very top: not in the shouty/sibilant 4–8 kHz area, but 10 kHz and above.

iem-letshuoer-ej07m.review: It's highly technical. The soundstage is super-duper open. Finally an electrostatic driver I like. A bit bright compared with the Tea Pro 2, with lower low-mids. Downside: not much low-mid bass, so the midrange is clean but lacks the energy of guitar twang and kick for rock. Sub-bass is boosted and still well balanced. Technically detailed. The imaging feels like it sits above your eyes, a bit outside. Outstanding MIDRANGE and vocal performance. Not harsh at all. Downside: the fit is awkward with the stock L-shaped cable. Superb clarity, superb detail, reverb tails, very clear instrument separation.

iem-ziigaat-arcanis.review: Very good timbre, very natural. A good close-to-neutral tuning. Very transparent and revealing mids, low to high: stunning and clean mids. A little too much in the highs for me, with bass a fair bit lower than the Tea Pro. So it's for people who like neutral with a bit of sparkle; not for bass lovers. Better timbre than the Tea Pro.

iem-thieaudio-hype-4.review: A mid-bass bump, good highs and upper mids. A safe tuning. Good value compared with the Hype, which isn't that different. But nowadays I prefer the Tea Pro: better separation, imaging and timbre, and its mid-bass to sub-bass is tidier.

iem-kiwi-ears-astral.review: Ugh, the pointiness is too noticeable. For me that's a no-go: no single frequency peak should stand out TOO much against the rest. And the top end here is too much for me. Even if you want a lot, it has to be as natural as the Tea Pro SE or Hisenior. Not for me. You will know: something is POINTY.

iem-crinear-daybreak.review: JM-1 / Meta tuning from the upper mids to the treble! Superb lower-treble performance around 4–6 kHz. Very resolving, not fatiguing at all, almost exactly the JM-1 treble roll-off. Very wide, open and spacious for the price; the treble and upper mids are very rich and resolving for the price. Highly coherent: everything feels unified, nothing sounds detached. A slightly laid-back presentation, not too forward for vocals and instruments, as if the mics were pulled back a little, giving a more distant sense of space. A really, really good IEM for just under 3 million rupiah.

iem-juzear-koto-nebula.tagline: King of separation at 2 million rupiah
iem-juzear-koto-nebula.review: Instrument separation, and the left-right spread, reach a bit further than the Daybreak and T6; both can still match its soundstage space. The main weakness is the timbre of the highs: still a bit metallic and crispy (even after EQ), so hi-hats and cymbals sound less natural. The kick has depth; the bass goes fairly deep too, wide and solid. Coherency is far above the Defiant: very unified.
